draft.title: Angles at the centre and circumference
card: Centre and circumference
An arc is part of a circle. Angles at the centre and at the circumference can both stand on the same arc. The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
Semicircle
If the arc is a semicircle, the angle at the centre is \(180^{\circ}\), so the angle at the circumference is half of that. An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
Same arc
Angles at the circumference standing on the same arc are equal. Each one is half the angle at the centre on that arc.
Example
The angle at the centre on an arc is \(80^{\circ}\). The angle at the circumference on the same arc is \(80^{\circ} \div 2 = 40^{\circ}\).

1.alt: A circle with centre O. Points A and B lie on the circle, and point C lies on the circle on the far side. Lines OA, OB, CA and CB are drawn. The angle at O is the angle at the centre and the angle at C is the angle at the circumference, both standing on arc AB.

draft.remember: Centre angle is double the circumference angle on the same arc.

a.q: O is the centre of a circle. Arc PQ makes an angle of \(140^{\circ}\) at O. What angle does arc PQ make at a point R on the circumference?
a.why: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre, so \(140^{\circ} \div 2 = 70^{\circ}\). Doubling to get \(280^{\circ}\) reverses the rule.
a.clue: Which angle is the larger one?

b.q: AB is a diameter of a circle. C is a point on the circle, and angle CAB is \(35^{\circ}\). What is angle ABC?
b.why: Angle ACB is in a semicircle, so it is \(90^{\circ}\). The angles of a triangle add to \(180^{\circ}\), so angle ABC is \(180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 35^{\circ} = 55^{\circ}\). Taking \(35^{\circ}\) wrongly treats the triangle as having two equal angles.
b.clue: Find the angle at C first.

proposal.title: Angles at the centre and circumference
card: Centre and circumference

An arc is part of a circle. An angle at the centre and an angle at the circumference can both stand on the same arc, with the point on the circumference on the rest of the circle. The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
Semicircle
If the arc is a semicircle, the angle at the centre is \(180^{\circ}\), so the angle at the circumference is half of that. An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
Same arc
Angles at the circumference standing on the same arc are equal. Each one is half the angle at the centre on that arc.
Example
The angle at the centre on an arc is \(80^{\circ}\). The angle at the circumference on the same arc is \(80^{\circ} \div 2 = 40^{\circ}\).
proposal.remember: Centre angle is double the circumference angle on the same arc.

a.q: O is the centre of a circle. Arc PQ makes an angle of \(140^{\circ}\) at O. R is on the circle, away from arc PQ. What is angle PRQ?
a.why: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre, so \(140^{\circ} \div 2 = 70^{\circ}\). Doubling to get \(280^{\circ}\) reverses the rule.
a.clue: Which angle is the larger one?

b.q: AB is a diameter of a circle. C is a point on the circle, and angle CAB is \(35^{\circ}\). What is angle ABC?
b.why: Angle ACB is in a semicircle, so it is \(90^{\circ}\). The angles of a triangle add to \(180^{\circ}\), so angle ABC is \(180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 35^{\circ} = 55^{\circ}\). Taking \(35^{\circ}\) wrongly treats the triangle as having two equal angles.
b.clue: Find the angle at C first.
